items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 12 at 12:05PM EST by NWS State College PA
items.description:
At 1205 PM EST, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from near Tremont to over Quarryville, moving
east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Myerstown, Rothsville, Pine Grove, Akron, Ephrata, Leola,
Strasburg, Newmanstown, Quarryville, Denver, Paradise, Reamstown,
New Holland, Minersville, Pottsville, Schuylkill Haven, St. Clair
and Orwigsburg.
items.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

items.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 12 at 12:31PM EST until November 12 at 3:45PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
items.description:
At 1231 PM EST, NJ511 reported flooding on NJ35 in Middletown
Township. All lanes were closed in the southbound direction at CR50
and New Monmouth Road. The northbound lanes south of Kings Highway
and Tindall Road were also closed.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Middletown, Tinton Falls, Red Bank, Keansburg, Lincroft and North
Middletown.
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 11:38AM EST until November 12 at 1:45PM EST by NWS Upton NY
items.areaDesc: Essex, NJ; Hudson, NJ; Union, NJ; Kings, NY; Richmond, NY
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Essex County in northeastern New Jersey...
Hudson County in northeastern New Jersey...
Southeastern Union County in northeastern New Jersey...
Kings (Brooklyn) County in southeastern New York...
Richmond (Staten Island) County in southeastern New York...

* WHEN...Until 145 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1137 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to showers
and embedded thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the advisory area.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 0.8 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Newark, Jersey City, Elizabeth, Flatbush, Bayonne, Linden, Coney
Island, Todt Hill, The Verrazano Narrows Bridge, Huguenot, Bay
Ridge, Port Richmond, Tottenville, Union and Tompkinsville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 8:28AM EST until November 12 at 2:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level in
low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.
items.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 12 at 9:40AM EST until November 13 at 6:00PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (3.2 to 11.6 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...Barnstable MA and Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Roads remain passable. Low lying areas and roads
near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy Street, may experience
pockets of shallow flooding less than one foot deep.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Splashover and very minor coastal flooding
are possible during the Friday afternoon high tide along north
facing beaches on Cape Cod Bay as well as Nantucket sound. No
significant impacts are expected and any splashover/very minor
coastal flooding will be quite short-lived, no more than an hour
on either side of high tide.
items.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 12 at 10:28AM EST until November 12 at 2:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Southern Fairfield County.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Brief minor flooding of the more vulnerable

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional minor coastal flooding will be

items.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 12:29PM EST until November 13 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Burlington VT
items.areaDesc: Western Essex; Eastern Addison; Eastern Rutland
items.description:
* WHAT...Wet snow expected mainly above 1200 feet. Total snow
accumulations between 2 and 4 inches.

* WHERE...In New York, Western Essex County. In Vermont, Eastern
Addison and Eastern Rutland Counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Thursday evening and Friday morning
commutes. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely
become slick and hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Impacts from snow will begin at higher
elevations today becoming more widespread in the Advisory areas
after 7 PM this evening as snow levels descend.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest on road
conditions in Vermont, visit https://newengland511.org and for New
York, visit https://511ny.org.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 12:27PM EST until November 13 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Albany NY
items.areaDesc: Hamilton; Northern Warren; Bennington; Western Windham
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Total snow accumulations up to 3 inches with isolated
totals of 3 to 5 inches for the highest mountain peaks.

* WHERE...Northern Warren and Hamilton Counties in New York and
elevations above 1500 feet in Bennington and Western Windham
Counties in Vermont.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.
